front: What percentage of the human body is water?
back: About 60% — the brain and heart are closer to 73% water.

front: How many hearts does an octopus have?
back: Three — two pump blood to the gills, one to the rest of the body.

front: What is the longest river in the world?
back: The Nile at 6,650 km (4,130 miles), though some argue the Amazon is longer depending on the source.

front: How fast does light travel in a vacuum?
What is the smallest country in the world by area?
back: Vatican City, at just 0.44 km² (110 acres).

front: How many bones does an adult human have?
back: 206. Babies are born with around 270 — many fuse together as we grow.

front: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
back: Diamond (score 10 on the Mohs hardness scale).

front: Which planet has the most moons?
back: Saturn, with 146 confirmed moons as of 2024.

front: What is a group of flamingos called?
back: A flamboyance. (A group of crows is called a murder.)

front: How long does it take sunlight to reach Earth?
back: About 8 minutes and 20 seconds, travelling 150 million km.

front: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
back: Nitrogen, at about 78%. Oxygen makes up about 21%.

front: How many colours are in a rainbow?
back: 7 — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet (ROY G BIV).

front: What is the largest organ in the human body?
back: The skin. In an adult it covers about 1.7–2 m² and weighs 3–4 kg.

front: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
back: 100°C (212°F). Higher altitude means lower pressure, so water boils at a lower temperature.

front: Which animal has the highest blood pressure?
back: The giraffe — its heart must pump blood up a very long neck, reaching ~280/180 mmHg.
